Santa Chimney Sweep evaluates the fireplace type, damaged components, and available repair options before recommending work. Masonry fireplaces and factory-built systems use different materials, so the repair approach must match the unit.
Our technicians review the fireplace type, reported problem, and available manufacturer or model information.
They begin by identifying whether the concern involves a masonry firebox, factory-built fireplace, gas appliance, or another supported component.

This helps determine which parts and repair methods may be appropriate.
Technicians examine the accessible areas connected to the reported problem.
For masonry fireplaces, they look for cracked firebricks, deteriorated mortar joints, and loose materials.

For factory-built fireplaces, they review damaged panels and supported components to determine whether compatible repairs or replacement parts are available.
The repair approach depends on the fireplace construction and condition of the affected materials.
Work may involve firebox masonry repair, replacement of damaged refractory panels, or other supported component repairs.

If the concern involves a gas fireplace, the model and affected components must be checked to confirm which work Santa Chimney Sweep can perform.
After the repair scope is approved, technicians complete the agreed work on the affected components.
The team reviews the completed repair and explains any additional concerns identified during the service.
If the problem also involves the chimney, flue, or another system, a separate inspection or service may be recommended.
